title: Enterprise Access Decision Tree: SLA thresholds, decision owners, and automated routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Define a deterministic decision tree and SLA thresholds for non-bug enterprise admin & access requests (RBAC, SSO/SAML, SCIM, org policies) that enables automated routing, clear owner assignment, and consistent prioritization. This ticket will produce: 1) a decision tree artifact that triages incoming requests into four outcome buckets (self-serve, triage + PM review, engineering work, security/legal review), 2) an SLA matrix tied to request severity and customer tier, 3) a lightweight evaluation checklist (scoring 0-10) for PMs/SEs to use during intake, and 4) routing rules (webhook/Linear automation spec) to push items to the right queue/team with suggested labels and initial estimates.
background: We continue to receive heterogeneous admin/access requests from enterprise customers — some are ask-for-guidance (self-serve), some require policy changes or new RBAC primitives, and others are infra-level (SCIM/SSO integration work). Current intake is ad hoc which causes delays and inconsistent SLAs across accounts. This initiative standardizes intake so enterprise customers get predictable timelines and internal owners get clear signals for scope and priority.
acceptance_criteria: Decision tree diagram checked into Confluence + exported PNG in drive with version tag
SLA matrix defined (P0..P3) mapping to response and resolution SLAs by customer tier (Self-Serve, Standard, Enterprise) with concrete hours/days
Evaluation checklist created and embedded as a PR template and intake form field (score 0-10) with guidance for each criterion
Automation spec (Linear workflow + webhook payload) submitted as draft PR for Eng to implement
At least one pilot customer request runs through the new flow end-to-end and meets SLA targets
Stakeholder sign-off from Security, Solutions Engineering, and Sales Ops documented in comments
intake_checklist: Requester: customer name, org ID, contact and account tier
Request type: RBAC | SSO/SAML hookup | SCIM provisioning | Org policy change
Business impact: user-facing outage, admin friction, compliance requirement, or enhancement
Scope: single customer config vs. platform-level change
Data sensitivity: PHI/PII or regulated data involved
Work required: config change | runbook update | engineering change | security review
decision_tree_summary: Step 1: If request is purely configuration (per-customer SSO/role mapping) and matches existing docs => Self-serve: send docs + 24h follow-up
Step 2: If request requires non-standard mapping (custom claims, delegated auth) but no infra change => Triage + SE assist (48h response, <7d resolution for standard customers)
Step 3: If request requires platform changes (new RBAC primitive, SCIM schema change, or migration) => Assign ENG owner, create scoped ticket, and apply SLA based on customer tier
Step 4: If request touches compliance/regulatory boundaries or encryption/KMS keys => Security & Legal review mandatory before ENG work
Step 5: Escalate to Account Exec for any request that would exceed planned committed delivery or require contract amendment
sla_matrix: P0 (Critical) - Enterprise: 4h response, 72h resolution (or rollback plan); Standard: 8h response, 96h resolution
P1 (High) - Enterprise: 24h response, 7d resolution; Standard: 48h response, 14d resolution
P2 (Medium) - Enterprise: 48h response, 30d resolution; Standard: 5d response, 45d resolution
P3 (Low) - Enterprise: 5d response, release-window delivery; Standard: 10d response, release-window delivery
routing_spec: If outcome = Self-serve -> auto-close with template message and attach docs; assign label 'self-serve'
If outcome = SE-assist -> route to solutions-engineering queue, add label 'triage-se' and assign initial estimate 3
If outcome = ENG-change -> create ENG ticket with component tag 'access' and link back to original; assign owner from rotation list
If security_review_required = true -> add 'security-review' label and notify security Slack channel + create task in Security queue
Automation payload sketch: {"key": "PM-<new>", "labels": ["triage", "admin-intake"], "initial_estimate": "3", "owner_queue": "se-queue"} (to be implemented by ENG)
implementation_notes: We will prototype the Linear automation using a webhook that accepts JSON and maps to fields; Eng needs to implement mapping for label sets and estimate presets
Solutions Engineering to author canonical KB articles for the top 5 recurring ask types; link those into the self-serve path
Rotation for ENG owners should be scoped to the 'access' component and integrated with on-call calendar to avoid ownerless tickets
Consider adding a triage UI field in console admin that captures the intake checklist to reduce back-and-forth
pilot_plan: Select 3 active enterprise customers with historical admin-intake volume for a two-week pilot
Run incoming requests through the new decision tree and collect metrics: time-to-response, time-to-resolution, and number of handoffs
Weekly stakeholder sync to surface friction and iterate on checklist language
Post-pilot retrospective to finalize SLA numbers and automation rules
